files.notes: The printed programme for the spring 2009 event series. The frame on the back is a detail from 'The Murerplan', which is a historic map of Zürich, printed by Jos Murer (1530–1580), 1576.

files.item: A flyer for Welcome To A World Of Paine, an event from Spring 2009 event series
files.notes: Incorporating the James Gillray (1756–1815) cartoon 'Fashion before Ease;—or,—A good Constitution sacrificed for a Fantastick Form'. Paine, who wrote The Rights of Man, started his working life as a corset maker.

files.item: A poster for Hillsborough: What Really Happened, an event which formed part of the Spring 2009 event series.
files.notes: '96' represents the number of people killed in the Hillsborough tragedy. The number was raised to 97 when the 97<sup>th</sup> Victim, Andrew Devine, died in July 2021.

files.item: A flyer for The Enemy Within, an event from Spring 2009.
files.notes: The background image is from the Battle of Orgreave, a clash between striking miners and police during the 1984–85 miner's strike.

files.item: A flyer for The Enemy Without, an event from the Spring 2009 event series.
files.notes: The 'NO NEW COAL' banner is from the Kingsnorth Climate camp in Kent, 2008.

files.item: A flyer for the Seven Stars plaque unveiling, which was part of the Spring 2009 event series.
files.notes: Adapted from a 'gallows ticket' for the execution of Jonathan Wild (1682 or 1683–1725), engraved by Thomas Cook (c.1744–1818). The gallows ticket is also used in the BRHG logo.

files.item: A flyer to advertise a raffle which raised funds for the Severn Stars plaque.
files.notes: The flyer depicts Thomas Clarkson, who started his research into slave ships while staying at The Seven Stars. BRHG raised money to erect a large plaque by Mike Baker (1961–2020) outside The Seven Stars.

files.item: A flyer for the Suffragette event, which was part of the Autumn 2009 event series
files.notes: Adapted from a postcard from approximately 1907, published by Millar & Lang, captioned 'Suffragettes: It's Love That Makes the World Go Round'. Churchill is taken from a photograph of Canadian Prime Minister Robert Borden and Winston Churchill (then First Lord of the Admiralty) in 1912. The substituting of a policeman for Winston Churchill is a reference to him being attacked by suffragette Theresa Garnett's attack, on November 15, 1909. The decretive frame is from The National American Woman Suffrage Association's 37th Convention Programme, 1905.

files.item: A 'business card' used to publicise BRHG, designed in 2009.
files.notes: The character of Death is from 'Death on the Barricade', part of The Dance of Death by Alfred Rethel (1816–1859), 1849. The BRHG logo is adapted from a 'gallows ticket' for the execution of Jonathan Wild (1682 or 1683–1725), engraved by Thomas Cook (c.1744–1818).

files.item: A poster for the BRHG events in New York in 2009.
files.notes: After the film poster for the original King Kong film, 1933. Kermit is a reference to the Muppet film The Muppets Take Manhattan, 1984. The figure with the hour glass is from Schachtafeln der Gesundheyt by Elluchasem Elimithar, 1533, illustrated by Hans Weiditz (1495–c.1537 ). The character with the dart, is from Le grant kalendrier, printed by Nicolas le Rouge, 1496.
